channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: Winners and losers in the coming AI margin collapse (part 2)
item.description: This article analyzes the shifting value distribution in the AI industry as inference costs plummet. It argues that hardware providers and consumers gain the most, while frontier labs must pivot toward complex agents to maintain a competitive advantage.

item.title: What’s an Icon in 2026?
item.description: This article explores the evolution of Apple app icons, which are shifting from static images to dynamic, multi-layered digital objects. It highlights how the new Icon Composer tool allows icons to be assembled on-the-fly by the operating system using layers and effects.

item.title: Mandatory Update: A Short Story
item.description: The author shares their recent venture into creative writing by joining a local fiction group. They have submitted a short story to the DEF CON 34 Creative Writing Short Story Contest.

item.title: Why don’t we just make the entire stack out of guard pages?
item.description: This post discusses the feasibility and architectural implications of implementing a software stack entirely composed of guard pages. It explores the technical constraints and potential outcomes of such a memory management strategy.

item.title: Pluralistic: Why aren't AI companies competing directly with their customers? (13 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow examines the paradoxical business models of AI companies, questioning why they prioritize selling infrastructure tools to customers rather than leveraging their technology to compete directly in those same markets. The post uses the metaphor of selling 'picks and shovels' to explore the dynamics of value, skepticism toward get-rich-quick schemes, and the underlying incentives of tech giants.

item.title: Control the ideas, not the code
item.description: The author argues that the essence of programming is shifting from manual coding to the conceptual control of ideas. He encourages developers to embrace AI-assisted workflows, noting that focusing too heavily on writing code often limits one's professional impact in an evolving landscape.

item.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
item.description: CISA recently addressed a significant security lapse where a contractor exposed internal credentials, including AWS Govcloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for six months. The incident highlights critical gaps in organizational response and vulnerability management that provide essential security lessons for all teams.

item.title: DOOMQL
item.description: DOOMQL is an experimental project that uses SQLite as a game engine to render a Doom-like game entirely through SQL queries. By leveraging recursive CTEs, the engine handles movement, combat, and rendering within the database, which can be further explored using Datasette.

item.title: datasette code-frequency chart on GitHub
item.description: Simon Willison examines his Datasette project's GitHub code frequency chart to analyze the impact of modern AI coding agents on his development output. The data reveals a significant spike in code additions correlating with the adoption of advanced models like Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6.

item.title: Directly Responsible Individuals (DRI)
item.description: The article defines the concept of a Directly Responsible Individual (DRI), a term originating from Apple to identify someone accountable for a project's success. It argues that while AI agents are useful, they cannot serve as DRIs because machines lack the capacity for true accountability.

item.title: shot-scraper 1.11
item.description: The shot-scraper 1.11 update introduces minor improvements to command consistency and server handling. Key changes include a new 30-second wait period for server startup and the addition of a --js-file option for loading JavaScript scripts.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.1.1
item.description: The sqlite-utils 4.1.1 release primarily addresses a transaction safety issue involving foreign key constraints during table transformations. It also introduces improved documentation cross-referencing between the CLI and Python API.

item.title: A dock that finally wakes up reliably
item.description: This post reviews a hardware docking station that solves common connectivity issues. It highlights the author's positive experience with a device that finally offers reliable wake-up functionality.

item.title: Don't you mean extinct?
item.description: This article discusses the nuances of terminology, specifically distinguishing between the concepts of obsolescence and extinction in technology. It explores how hardware and software lifecycles are perceived by users compared to their actual functional states.

item.title: I love LLMs, I hate hype
item.description: The author expresses genuine enthusiasm for AI technological progress while criticizing the industry's pervasive, fear-based hype. They argue that AI development is driven by general computing progress rather than the proprietary efforts of frontier labs, which they believe struggle to capture the value they create.

item.title: Posterior variance
item.description: This article explores the counterintuitive statistical phenomenon where adding more data does not always decrease posterior variance. It references previous analysis of Bayesian models to illustrate how posterior means behave as weighted averages.

item.title: Posterior mean
item.description: This article explores the concept of the posterior mean in Bayesian statistics, which acts as a compromise between prior beliefs and new observed data. It explains how to mathematically balance previous information with fresh evidence to update judgments.

item.title: Another Ridiculous Interrail Holiday - 6,379Km and 13 Countries over 7 weeks
item.description: The author shares their experience of a 6,379km Interrail trip across 13 countries over seven weeks. By adjusting their pass strategy from a previous month-long intensive trip to a more relaxed two-month plan, they successfully managed a long-distance European journey including ferry travel.

item.title: Making cooled clothing:
item.description: This post explores the engineering challenges of designing wearable cooling systems. It compares active refrigeration methods, like semiconductor cooling, with phase-change materials and concludes by evaluating specific chemical compounds for personal thermal regulation.

item.title: Fable gets another bump
item.description: Anthropic has extended access to the Claude Fable model due to ongoing compute constraints, while OpenAI has removed usage limits for their GPT-5.6 model. Simon Willison argues that Anthropic should permanently integrate Fable into their plans to remain competitive against OpenAI's more accessible approach.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.1
item.description: sqlite-utils 4.1 has been released, introducing a new --code option for the insert and upsert CLI commands. This feature allows users to provide blocks of Python code to generate rows directly, extending the tool's existing capabilities for data manipulation.

item.title: Goede geluiden over digitale autonomie
item.description: The Dutch government is shifting its stance on digital autonomy, moving from a decade of denial to actively publishing documents that prioritize independence. These recent official texts suggest a newfound commitment to digital sovereignty and concrete decision-making.

item.title: Dot product: Component vs. Geometric definition
item.description: This article explores the mathematical equivalence between the algebraic component definition and the geometric definition of the vector dot product. It provides formal proofs for this relationship using the law of cosines and vector projections.

item.title: AI 2040 and the Cult of Intelligence
item.description: The author critiques the 'hard takeoff' theory of AI, arguing that theoretical intelligence cannot bypass the physical constraints and logistical complexities of real-world engineering. They emphasize that physical reality, such as supply chains and hardware durability, remains a significant bottleneck that tokens alone cannot resolve.

item.title: Reading List 07/11/26
item.description: This post provides a curated collection of diverse news topics, ranging from socioeconomic shifts and corporate financial performance to infrastructure challenges and technological developments. It serves as a brief overview of current events and systemic issues across various sectors.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 11 July 2026
item.description: This roundup covers the latest updates in package management as of July 11, 2026. Key releases include major breaking changes in npm 12.0.0, new registry configuration features in pnpm, security and performance improvements in uv, and various updates for Go, Rust, and winget.

item.title: Prefer STRICT tables in SQLite
item.description: This article advocates for using SQLite's 'STRICT' table feature to enforce rigid data typing. By enabling this option, developers can prevent common errors such as inserting invalid data types into columns and defining tables with incorrect types.

item.title: Progress on Gilbreath’s conjecture
item.description: The article revisits Gilbreath’s conjecture, a mathematical problem involving prime number sequences. It highlights the simplicity and unusual nature of the conjecture, noting historical interest from mathematicians like Paul Erdős.

item.title: Pluralistic: Workplace "flexibility" isn't (11 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: The article critiques the gig economy, arguing that corporate claims of 'flexibility' are actually a method for shifting risks onto workers. It highlights the irony that while these data-driven companies possess granular information on worker earnings and unpaid time, they deliberately keep this data private to obscure their labor practices.

item.title: In defense of not understanding your codebase
item.description: This article argues that it is acceptable and sometimes beneficial for developers to have an incomplete understanding of their entire codebase. It suggests that cognitive focus should be prioritized over the pressure to master every line of system code.

item.title: This Week on The Analog Antiquarian
item.description: This entry explores the historical and digital significance of 'Henry VI, Part 3,' the fourth installment in a series examining classic software titles. It contextualizes the game's development and its place within the broader landscape of early computing history.

item.title: Adam Brown – A deep but accessible introduction to general relativity
item.description: This episode features Adam Brown providing an accessible yet deep introduction to the principles of general relativity. The discussion specifically explores how the unique properties of black holes position them as the ultimate theoretical power plants.

item.title: Package Management as Org Chart
item.description: This post explores the relationship between dependency management tools and organizational structures, applying Conway’s Law to various package management strategies. It illustrates how technical resolution rules, such as monorepos or explicit build definitions, mirror the internal communication and decision-making hierarchies of engineering teams.

item.title: The case of the mysterious changes to integers when there shouldn’t have been any code generation effect
item.description: This post investigates a technical mystery where integer values were unexpectedly altered despite no apparent changes in code generation. The author analyzes the underlying mechanics to determine the source of these silent modifications.

item.title: Game Review: Lovers In A Dangerous Spacetime ★★★☆☆
item.description: The author reviews the cooperative game 'Lovers in a Dangerous Spacetime' as part of a New Year's resolution to play more games with his wife. He appreciates the game's cooperative focus over competitive gameplay and finds its length appropriate for casual play.

item.title: The Tadpole galaxy:
item.description: This post presents an astrophotography capture of the Tadpole galaxy (Arp 188), discussing its unique tidal tail and potential companion galaxy. It provides technical details on the imaging setup, exposure data, and the specific processing workflow used to create the final image.

item.title: Pluralistic: "Rights for robots" and the AI slavery fantasy (10 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques the AI boom as an ideological project driven by the desire to eliminate human friction from the workplace. He argues that corporations prioritize automation not just for efficiency, but to avoid the complexities and dissent inherent in managing human labor.

item.title: Quoting Nilay Patel
item.description: Nilay Patel argues that the hardware limitations of augmented reality glasses necessitate constant cloud-based data processing, creating an inevitable conflict with user privacy. He suggests that the societal costs of these trade-offs may be too high, potentially warranting a halt to the development of such devices.

item.title: Quoting OpenAI
item.description: Simon Willison highlights the confusion surrounding OpenAI's ChatGPT Work feature. He notes that the official documentation fails to clearly explain how data syncs between cloud, web, and desktop versions.

item.title: QuadRF can spot drones and see WiFi through my wall
item.description: The QuadRF is a powerful phased-array radio device utilizing a Raspberry Pi 5 and FPGA technology to perform advanced signal processing. It demonstrates the capability to track drones and intercept WiFi traffic through walls, highlighting significant privacy and security concerns regarding wireless signals.

item.title: Boxed In
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article explores the career limitations that arise when creators impose overly rigid constraints on their work. Using Paul Fusco and his character ALF as a case study, it illustrates how an uncompromising commitment to maintaining an illusion can stifle production and hinder long-term professional opportunities.

item.title: Unboxed: Zig
item.description: This article provides an analytical overview of the Zig programming language's built-in package manager. It explains the roles of the build.zig and build.zig.zon files, detailing how Zig manages dependencies through content hashes and restricted object notation.

item.title: I’ve decoded a #pragma detect_mismatch error and fixed the mismatch, but I still get the error
item.description: This post explains that fixing a #pragma detect_mismatch error requires more than just changing the code. You must perform a full rebuild of all project dependencies to ensure the fix propagates correctly.

item.title: The console wars have been lost
item.description: The blog post argues that Valve has effectively won the console wars through passive strategy. Rather than competing directly with traditional console manufacturers, Valve focused on building an open, hardware-agnostic platform.

item.title: Arp 90
item.description: This post provides technical imaging details and processing steps for the interacting galaxy pair Arp 90. It includes specific gear configurations, exposure data, and a summary of the image calibration and stacking workflow.

item.title: Pluralistic: Post-political (09 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques the concept of post-politics and the 'horseshoe theory,' arguing that these ideas create a dangerous false equivalence between left and right. He asserts that modern political divisions represent substantive, life-and-death disagreements rather than mere tribalism or cultural signaling.

item.title: The new GPT-5.6 family: Luna, Terra, Sol
item.description: OpenAI has released the GPT-5.6 family of models, including Luna, Terra, and Sol, which feature a 1-million-token context window and improved agentic performance. While these models offer significant cost efficiencies and high scores on long-running workflow benchmarks, they demonstrate varied performance on coding tasks like SWE-Bench Pro.

item.title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1
item.description: Simon Willison introduces Muse Spark 1.1, Meta's latest model featuring enhanced agentic tool use and an official API. The post highlights the model's evaluation findings and provides a practical guide for accessing it via a new CLI plugin.

item.title: llm-meta-ai 0.1
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.1 of llm-meta-ai. This tool enables users to run prompts against Meta's new muse-spark-1.1 model using the LLM command-line interface.

item.title: llm 0.31.1
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.31.1 of the LLM command-line utility. This update specifically resolves a JSON error that occurred when OpenAI Chat Completion endpoints returned empty tool call arguments.

item.title: Rewriting Bun in Rust
item.description: Bun creator Jarred Sumner details the decision to rewrite the Bun runtime from Zig to Rust to solve complex memory management issues. The article explores how AI-powered coding agents made this massive, historically discouraged undertaking possible by automating the translation and verification process.

item.title: Introducing GPT‑Live
item.description: Simon Willison reviews the newly released GPT-Live for ChatGPT voice mode, highlighting its improved reasoning capabilities and ability to delegate complex tasks to GPT-5.5. He shares his personal experience with the model, noting its enhanced conversational flow and documenting an interesting anecdote regarding unexpected model behavior.

item.title: The Decline of Deviance 2
item.description: This article explores the shifting social dynamics regarding non-conformity and individual expression in contemporary culture. It analyzes how societal standards of deviance have evolved and what this means for personal authenticity.

item.title: Weekly Update 511: Live from my Riad in Marrakech
item.description: Troy Hunt shares a personal update from Marrakech while addressing the ongoing challenge of data breach management. He uses the metaphor of trying to remove urine from a swimming pool to illustrate the difficulty of containing leaked personal information.

item.title: Family Feud: Mac-assed Mac App Edition
item.description: This post uses a 'Family Feud' game show format to critique why large, wealthy tech companies often release 'Electron' apps instead of high-quality, native macOS applications. The author suggests a correlation between corporate size and the tendency to prioritize cross-platform convenience over a true native user experience.

item.title: The other kind of control flow guard check: The combined validate and call
item.description: This post discusses a specific optimization in Control Flow Guard (CFG) mechanisms where validation and function calls are combined into a single operation. It explains how this dual-purpose approach streamlines security checks in system programming.

item.title: Agents are monads (but not that kind)
item.description: The article explores the conceptual relationship between software agents and monads. It humorously attempts to explain complex functional programming abstractions without relying on heavy academic jargon like endofunctors.

item.title: A bug which only affected left-handed users
item.description: The author shares a humorous reflection on a bug report that specifically affected left-handed users. The post highlights the often-overlooked considerations in user experience design and the challenges of reporting niche accessibility issues.

item.title: And Then the Billionaire Paid Off $550 Million of Our Debts
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The article examines the complexities behind billionaire philanthropy, using Evan Spiegel's donation to medical debt and Bill Gates' foundation as examples. The author argues that public acts of charity often come with nuances and structural motives that merit closer scrutiny.

item.title: Felons, Fraudsters Flog Offensive Cybersecurity Startup
item.description: An investigative report reveals that a cybersecurity startup purchasing zero-day vulnerabilities is led by convicted felons with a history of fraudulent business activities. The article exposes the founders' backgrounds, including their involvement in fake intelligence companies and far-right conspiracy theories.

item.title: Quoting Kenton Varda
item.description: Kenton Varda has implemented a moratorium on AI-generated change descriptions within his team's workflow. He argues that AI output often redundantly describes code details while failing to provide the essential high-level context required for effective code reviews.

item.title: The Special Value Pi 4 was extremely short-lived
item.description: Jeff Geerling highlights the discovery and acquisition of a rare 'Special Value' Raspberry Pi 4 edition. This limited model features a lower-clocked processor of 1.25 GHz compared to the standard retail version's 1.8 GHz.

item.title: My blog has moved
item.description: The author provides a notice that their blog has migrated to a new platform. They include a link to the new location and provide an updated RSS feed for existing subscribers to follow.

item.title: Kort geding aandeelhouders Solvinity
item.description: The author recounts their firsthand observations from the Solvinity shareholders' lawsuit against the Dutch government regarding a blocked sale to a US firm. They note discrepancies between the courtroom events and the subsequent media coverage by major news outlets.

item.title: A full body MRI earns you a year of smoking
item.description: This article explores the concept of radiation exposure by equating the dosage received from a full-body MRI to equivalent risks in other activities. It uses provocative comparisons to put medical imaging risks into perspective against common or extreme life experiences.

item.title: Content addressing in package managers
item.description: This article explores the implementation of content addressing in modern package managers, where data is identified by cryptographic hashes rather than locations. It surveys various systems that utilize content-addressable storage for files, layers, and artifacts to improve deduplication, security, and verification.

item.title: How did Windows 95 decide that a setup program ran?
item.description: This post explains the technical heuristics used by Windows 95 to identify when a setup program was running. It provides historical insight into the operating system's internal detection mechanisms.

item.title: Pluralistic: How US states and international trustbusters can beat Big Tech (07 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This article examines the global trend of antitrust enforcement against Big Tech, highlighting the collaborative efforts between US regulators and international authorities. It posits that a shared commitment to aggressive antitrust policy is essential to curbing the power of major technology corporations.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0, now with database schema migrations
item.description: Simon Willison has released sqlite-utils 4.0, a major update introducing database schema migrations, nested transactions, and support for compound foreign keys. The release highlights the powerful table.transform() method, which enables complex schema modifications beyond standard SQLite capabilities.

item.title: sqlite-migrate 0.2
item.description: The sqlite-migrate library has been updated to version 0.2, which officially retires the standalone package. It now functions as a compatibility shim to support the newly released sqlite-utils 4.0 dependency.

item.title: github-code Web Component
item.description: Simon Willison introduces an experimental Web Component, github-code, created using AI to embed specific sections of GitHub files into web pages. The tool fetches raw code from GitHub based on provided URLs and renders it with line numbers.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0
item.description: sqlite-utils 4.0 has been released, introducing support for database schema migrations. This update enhances the tool's capabilities for managing and evolving SQLite database structures.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc4
item.description: Simon Willison has released sqlite-utils 4.0rc4, which serves as the final release candidate before the stable 4.0 version. This update primarily incorporates feedback provided during a detailed review by Claude Fable 5.

item.title: tencent/Hy3
item.description: Tencent has released Hy3, a new 295B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model featuring a 256K context window and Apache 2.0 licensing. The model demonstrates high performance in productivity tasks and is currently available for testing via OpenRouter.

item.title: Blog about things you don't understand yet
item.description: This article discusses the intellectual benefit of engaging with topics that currently elude your understanding. It highlights the importance of curiosity and the mental growth that comes from tackling complex, unfamiliar subjects.

item.title: GLM 5.2 and the coming AI margin collapse (part 1)
item.description: The article introduces GLM 5.2 as a powerful open-weights model capable of matching top-tier competitors like GPT and Opus for agentic tasks. It suggests that this performance at a significantly lower price point signals an impending collapse in AI inference profit margins.

item.title: Making a Shuffle Button
item.description: The author describes the challenge of implementing a 'Shuffle' button on a static blog, specifically the inefficiencies of embedding all post IDs into every page using JavaScript. He seeks a more performant, non-JS alternative to avoid unnecessary rebuilds and cache invalidation caused by frequent content updates.

item.title: Reproducing a geometry theorem diagram
item.description: The author explores the process of programmatically recreating a specific geometry theorem diagram using coordinates and mathematical assumptions. By defining the unit circle and the perpendicular line CD, the post details the steps taken to plot the geometric components accurately.

item.title: e approximation
item.description: This article explores a highly accurate fractional approximation of the mathematical constant e (2721/1001). It contrasts this specific approximation with simpler methods, highlighting how such fractions can provide greater precision than standard decimal truncations.

item.title: I opened a file with FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE, but now I changed my mind
item.description: This post explains that the FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE flag cannot be removed once a file is opened with it. It suggests that if you need to retain the file, you must adopt a different approach to file handling.

item.title: Life with hazard ratios
item.description: The article explains why hazard ratios in health studies are often misinterpreted as direct indicators of life expectancy changes. Through the use of hypothetical models like Russian roulette, it demonstrates that the impact of a hazard ratio depends heavily on the baseline mortality rate and the age at which risks occur.

item.title: I'm just so bored of AI
item.description: The author expresses growing fatigue with the constant hype surrounding artificial intelligence, comparing it to repetitive and tedious conversations about fleeting trends. They argue that the novelty of AI-driven automation is quickly wearing off, leading to a sense of exhaustion with current tech discourse.

item.title: Stephan's Quintet
item.description: This post provides a deep-sky analysis of Stephan's Quintet, noting that the blue spiral galaxy is a foreground object rather than a true member of the group. It details the technical configuration and processing workflow used to capture this image of the Hickson Compact Group 92.

item.title: Amazon Basics, but for intellectual property.
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: This article discusses the conflict of interest inherent in Amazon's business model, where the platform leverages proprietary sales data to replicate successful third-party products under its Amazon Basics brand. It highlights how merchants are forced to expose their operational data to Amazon to reach customers, despite Amazon's denials regarding the misuse of private seller information.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc3
item.description: Simon Willison has released sqlite-utils 4.0rc3, introducing support for compound foreign keys and updated case-insensitive column matching. This release incorporates various bug fixes and improvements as the project nears its stable 4.0 version.

item.title: C2PA only works if everything is signed
item.description: This article examines the limitations of the C2PA standard, arguing that its effectiveness depends entirely on universal adoption and consistent signing across the entire digital content lifecycle. It highlights how gaps in the verification chain can compromise the integrity and trustworthiness of media provenance.

item.title: Travel notes: PLDI Boulder
item.description: Max Bernstein reflects on his fourth PLDI conference experience in Boulder, highlighting the value of networking, research discussions, and workshops. He notes specific technical insights gained from the EGRAPHS workshop and casual interactions with fellow researchers.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2, mostly written by Claude Fable (for about $149.25)
item.description: Simon Willison uses the AI tool Claude Fable to conduct a final code review of sqlite-utils 4.0rc1 before the stable release. The process successfully identified critical bugs, including a serious data integrity issue with delete_where(), helping ensure a more robust version 4.0.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2
item.description: Simon Willison has announced the release of sqlite-utils 4.0rc2. A significant portion of this version was developed with the assistance of the AI model Claude Fable.

item.title: Building a World Map with only 500 bytes
item.description: This post highlights an innovative technique for generating an ASCII world map using just 445 bytes of data. It demonstrates how to leverage deflate compression and JavaScript's fetch API with data URIs to achieve highly efficient text rendering.

item.title: Better Models: Worse Tools
item.description: The article discusses a regression where newer Claude models struggle with tool-use schemas compared to older versions. It suggests that models are becoming overly optimized for specific vendor-provided tools, leading to compatibility issues with third-party coding harnesses.

item.title: Reading List 07/04/26
item.description: This digest covers a diverse range of topics, including the prevalence of households without homeowners insurance and the implications of AI chip smuggling. It also explores technical and business developments such as Japan’s unique dual-frequency electrical grid and Meta's current strategy in the AI computing sector.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 4 July 2026
item.description: This weekly digest covers key updates across various package managers including Hex, Conan, uv, pixi, mise, Rust/Cargo, npm, and Homebrew. The releases focus on security enhancements, dependency policy management, SBOM improvements, and performance optimizations.

item.title: Does additional data always reduce posterior variance?
item.description: This post examines the counterintuitive Bayesian scenario where collecting additional data does not always result in a decreased posterior variance. It explores the theoretical conditions under which new information might fail to narrow confidence intervals.

item.title: Better Models: Worse Tools
item.description: The author discusses a regression where newer Claude models, specifically Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5, are more prone to generating malformed tool calls compared to their predecessors. He explains that tool calling relies on text-based signals and emphasizes that despite model advancements, schema compliance for structured outputs remains a significant challenge.

item.title: Combined 1D and 2D Barcodes
item.description: The author explores the transition from traditional 1D barcodes to 2D QR codes by creating a hybrid design. By embedding a UPC within a QR code, the system allows for dual-mode scanning depending on the proximity of the reading device.

item.title: Swimming Pools, Pee, and Trying to Delete Your Data From the Internet
item.description: The article uses the analogy of urinating in a swimming pool to explain the near-impossibility of completely deleting one's personal data from the internet. It highlights how once information is shared or copied, it becomes permanently diffused across the digital ecosystem.

item.title: The Life and Times of Maxis, Part 1: SimEverything
item.description: This article explores the early history of Maxis Software and the visionary thinking of its co-founder, Will Wright. It highlights the company's unique approach to simulation games and the role of gaming enthusiasts in preserving the history of the medium.

item.title: The Fall and Rise of Screwworm
item.description: This article explores the historical impact and life cycle of the screwworm, a devastating parasite that affected livestock across North America. It details how these pests seasonally migrated from southern regions, highlighting their historical prevalence before eradication efforts.

item.title: How did we conclude that CcNamespace.dll was the ringleader of a group of DLLs that unloaded prematurely?
item.description: This post explains the investigative process used to identify CcNamespace.dll as the primary cause behind the premature unloading of a group of DLLs. It highlights the importance of analyzing contextual clues to diagnose complex system behavior issues.
